the hydrocarbon chain structure has a major influence on the internal dimensions of the L(alpha), H(II), and L(alpha)/H(I) phase transition regions of these PEs, and that this influence depends on the temperature and on the phase in which the PE is found.
the L(alpha)/ H(II) transition temperature is not a constant for a given lipid but depends on the structure of its hydrocarbon chains.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the L(alpha)/ H(II) transition is not a simple two-state transition but is rather a complex, multi-step process that involves the cooperative rearrangement of the entire lipid bilayer, including the hydrocarbon chains and the lipid headgroups, and that involves the cooperative motion of water molecules as well.

the L(alpha) to H(II) transition is a continuous process that involves a progressive increase in the average lipid length and headgroup area, and a progressive decrease in the water layer thickness and d-spacing, as the temperature increases through T(h).
the structures of the L(alpha), H(II), and the transition region are strongly affected by the structure of the hydrocarbon chains of the phospholipids.
